stated: The Conservative Party will protect the laws ensuring Right to Buy discounts rise with inflation and fight any plans by local authorities to abolish Right to Buy.

source.quote: We will protect the laws that ensure the discounts rise with inflation and fight any plan by local authorities to abolish the Right to Buy altogether.

bearing_set.reason: Protecting Right to Buy discounts directly affects the social/affordable housing stock (homes sold leave the tenure permanently) and the affordability of home-ownership for existing council tenants — a real, contested trade-off at the heart of the affordable housing fundamental.

Maintaining inflation-linked discounts means continued disposal of public assets at below-market value, shrinking local-authority balance sheets and reducing their capacity to fund replacement stock — a concrete fiscal mechanism tied to the debt-path and asset-sustainability indicators.

RTB transfers discounted housing wealth to sitting tenants (typically lower-income but housed), while reducing stock available to those on waiting lists (often the most deprived); the distributional direction is genuinely contested, earning a real mixed verdict on who gains and who loses.

membership_note: O1 is the primary bearing (stock vs. access tradeoff); O12 captures the below-market public-asset disposal cost; O14 reflects the intra-lower-income distributional split. O11 was considered but the discount is a housing transfer, not a change to the tax burden on earnings.
